# czlonkowski/n8n-mcp 5578f73c380c MIT
ok # Complete Guide to AI Agents in n8n\n\nThis comprehensive guide covers everything you need to build production-ready AI Agent workflows in n8n.\n\n## Table of Contents\n1. [AI Agent Architecture](#architecture)\n2. [Essential Connection Types](#connections)\n3. [Building Your First AI Agent](#first-agent)\n4. [AI Tools Deep Dive](#tools)\n5. [Advanced Patterns](#advanced)\n6. [Validation & Best Practices](#validation)\n7. [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)\n\n---\n\n## 1. AI Agent Architecture {#architecture}\n\n### Core Components\n\nAn n8n AI Agent workflow typically consists of:\n\n1. **Chat Trigger**: Entry point for user interactions\n   - Webhook-based or manual trigger\n   - Supports streaming responses (responseMode)\n   - Passes user message to AI Agent\n\n2. **AI Agent**: The orchestrator\n   - Manages conversation flow\n   - Decides when to use tools\n   - Iterates until task is complete\n   - Supports fallback models for reliability\n\n3. **Language Model**: The AI brain\n   - OpenAI GPT-4, Claude, Gemini, etc.\n   - Connected via ai_languageModel port\n   - Can have primary + fallback for reliability\n\n4. **Tools**: AI Agent's capabilities\n   - HTTP Request, Code, Vector Store, etc.\n   - Connected via ai_tool port\n   - Each tool needs clear toolDescription\n\n5. **Optional Components**:\n   - Memory (conversation history)\n   - Output Parser (structured responses)\n   - Vector Store (knowledge retrieval)\n\n### Connection Flow\n\n**CRITICAL**: AI connections flow TO the consumer (reversed from standard n8n):\n\n```\nStandard n8n:  [Source] --main--> [Target]\nAI pattern:    [Language Model] --ai_languageModel--> [AI Agent]\n               [HTTP Tool] --ai_tool--> [AI Agent]\n```\n\nThis is why you use `sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel"` when connecting components.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Essential Connection Types {#connections}\n\n### The 8 AI Connection Types\n\n1. **ai_languageModel**\n   - FROM: OpenAI Chat Model, Anthropic, Google Gemini, etc.\n   - TO: AI Agent, Basic LLM Chain\n   - REQUIRED: Every AI Agent needs 1-2 language models\n   - Example: `{type: "addConnection", source: "OpenAI", target: "AI Agent", sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel"}`\n\n2. **ai_tool**\n   - FROM: Any tool node (HTTP Request Tool, Code Tool, etc.)\n   - TO: AI Agent\n   - REQUIRED: At least 1 tool recommended\n   - Example: `{type: "addConnection", source: "HTTP Request Tool", target: "AI Agent", sourceOutput: "ai_tool"}`\n\n3. **ai_memory**\n   - FROM: Window Buffer Memory, Conversation Summary, etc.\n   - TO: AI Agent\n   - OPTIONAL: 0-1 memory system\n   - Enables conversation history tracking\n\n4. **ai_outputParser**\n   - FROM: Structured Output Parser, JSON Parser, etc.\n   - TO: AI Agent\n   - OPTIONAL: For structured responses\n   - Must set hasOutputParser=true on AI Agent\n\n5. **ai_embedding**\n   - FROM: Embeddings OpenAI, Embeddings Google, etc.\n   - TO: Vector Store (Pinecone, In-Memory, etc.)\n   - REQUIRED: For vector-based retrieval\n\n6. **ai_vectorStore**\n   - FROM: Vector Store node\n   - TO: Vector Store Tool\n   - REQUIRED: For retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)\n\n7. **ai_document**\n   - FROM: Document Loader, Default Data Loader\n   - TO: Vector Store\n   - REQUIRED: Provides data for vector storage\n\n8. **ai_textSplitter**\n   - FROM: Text Splitter nodes\n   - TO: Document processing chains\n   - OPTIONAL: Chunk large documents\n\n### Connection Examples\n\n```typescript\n// Basic AI Agent setup\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  id: "workflow_id",\n  operations: [\n    // Connect language model (REQUIRED)\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "OpenAI Chat Model",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel"\n    },\n    // Connect tools\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "HTTP Request Tool",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_tool"\n    },\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "Code Tool",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_tool"\n    },\n    // Add memory (optional)\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "Window Buffer Memory",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_memory"\n    }\n  ]\n})\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Building Your First AI Agent {#first-agent}\n\n### Step-by-Step Tutorial\n\n#### Step 1: Create Chat Trigger\n\nUse `n8n_create_workflow` or manually create a workflow with:\n\n```typescript\n{\n  name: "My First AI Agent",\n  nodes: [\n    {\n      id: "chat_trigger",\n      name: "Chat Trigger",\n      type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.chatTrigger",\n      position: [100, 100],\n      parameters: {\n        options: {\n          responseMode: "lastNode"  // or "streaming" for real-time\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  ],\n  connections: {}\n}\n```\n\n#### Step 2: Add Language Model\n\n```typescript\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  id: "workflow_id",\n  operations: [\n    {\n      type: "addNode",\n      node: {\n        name: "OpenAI Chat Model",\n        type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.lmChatOpenAi",\n        position: [300, 50],\n        parameters: {\n          model: "gpt-4",\n          temperature: 0.7\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n})\n```\n\n#### Step 3: Add AI Agent\n\n```typescript\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  id: "workflow_id",\n  operations: [\n    {\n      type: "addNode",\n      node: {\n        name: "AI Agent",\n        type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agent",\n        position: [300, 150],\n        parameters: {\n          promptType: "auto",\n          systemMessage: "You are a helpful assistant. Be concise and accurate."\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n})\n```\n\n#### Step 4: Connect Components\n\n```typescript\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  id: "workflow_id",\n  operations: [\n    // Chat Trigger → AI Agent (main connection)\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "Chat Trigger",\n      target: "AI Agent"\n    },\n    // Language Model → AI Agent (AI connection)\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "OpenAI Chat Model",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel"\n    }\n  ]\n})\n```\n\n#### Step 5: Validate\n\n```typescript\nn8n_validate_workflow({id: "workflow_id"})\n```\n\n---\n\n## 4. AI Tools Deep Dive {#tools}\n\n### Tool Types and When to Use Them\n\n#### 1. HTTP Request Tool\n**Use when**: AI needs to call external APIs\n\n**Critical Requirements**:\n- `toolDescription`: Clear, 15+ character description\n- `url`: API endpoint (can include placeholders)\n- `placeholderDefinitions`: Define all {placeholders}\n- Proper authentication if needed\n\n**Example**:\n```typescript\n{\n  type: "addNode",\n  node: {\n    name: "GitHub Issues Tool",\n    type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolHttpRequest",\n    position: [500, 100],\n    parameters: {\n      method: "POST",\n      url: "https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues",\n      toolDescription: "Create GitHub issues. Requires owner (username), repo (repository name), title, and body.",\n      placeholderDefinitions: {\n        values: [\n          {name: "owner", description: "Repository owner username"},\n          {name: "repo", description: "Repository name"},\n          {name: "title", description: "Issue title"},\n          {name: "body", description: "Issue description"}\n        ]\n      },\n      sendBody: true,\n      jsonBody: "={{ { title: $json.title, body: $json.body } }}"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n#### 2. Code Tool\n**Use when**: AI needs to run custom logic\n\n**Critical Requirements**:\n- `name`: Function name (alphanumeric + underscore)\n- `description`: 10+ character explanation\n- `code`: JavaScript or Python code\n- `inputSchema`: Define expected inputs (recommended)\n\n**Example**:\n```typescript\n{\n  type: "addNode",\n  node: {\n    name: "Calculate Shipping",\n    type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.toolCode",\n    position: [500, 200],\n    parameters: {\n      name: "calculate_shipping",\n      description: "Calculate shipping cost based on weight (kg) and distance (km)",\n      language: "javaScript",\n      code: "const cost = 5 + ($input.weight * 2) + ($input.distance * 0.1); return { cost };",\n      specifyInputSchema: true,\n      inputSchema: "{ \\"type\\": \\"object\\", \\"properties\\": { \\"weight\\": { \\"type\\": \\"number\\" }, \\"distance\\": { \\"type\\": \\"number\\" } } }"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n#### 3. Vector Store Tool\n**Use when**: AI needs to search knowledge base\n\n**Setup**: Requires Vector Store + Embeddings + Documents\n\n**Example**:\n```typescript\n// Step 1: Create Vector Store with embeddings and documents\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  operations: [\n    {type: "addConnection", source: "Embeddings OpenAI", target: "Pinecone", sourceOutput: "ai_embedding"},\n    {type: "addConnection", source: "Document Loader", target: "Pinecone", sourceOutput: "ai_document"}\n  ]\n})\n\n// Step 2: Connect Vector Store to Vector Store Tool\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  operations: [\n    {type: "addConnection", source: "Pinecone", target: "Vector Store Tool", sourceOutput: "ai_vectorStore"}\n  ]\n})\n\n// Step 3: Connect tool to AI Agent\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  operations: [\n    {type: "addConnection", source: "Vector Store Tool", target: "AI Agent", sourceOutput: "ai_tool"}\n  ]\n})\n```\n\n#### 4. AI Agent Tool (Sub-Agents)\n**Use when**: Need specialized expertise\n\n**Example**: Research specialist sub-agent\n```typescript\n{\n  type: "addNode",\n  node: {\n    name: "Research Specialist",\n    type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.agentTool",\n    position: [500, 300],\n    parameters: {\n      name: "research_specialist",\n      description: "Expert researcher that searches multiple sources and synthesizes information. Use for detailed research tasks.",\n      systemMessage: "You are a research specialist. Search thoroughly, cite sources, and provide comprehensive analysis."\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n#### 5. MCP Client Tool\n**Use when**: Need to use Model Context Protocol servers\n\n**Example**: Filesystem access\n```typescript\n{\n  type: "addNode",\n  node: {\n    name: "Filesystem Tool",\n    type: "@n8n/n8n-nodes-langchain.mcpClientTool",\n    position: [500, 400],\n    parameters: {\n      description: "Access file system to read files, list directories, and search content",\n      mcpServer: {\n        transport: "stdio",\n        command: "npx",\n        args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/allowed/path"]\n      },\n      tool: "read_file"\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Advanced Patterns {#advanced}\n\n### Pattern 1: Streaming Responses\n\nFor real-time user experience:\n\n```typescript\n// Set Chat Trigger to streaming mode\n{\n  parameters: {\n    options: {\n      responseMode: "streaming"\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// CRITICAL: AI Agent must NOT have main output connections in streaming mode\n// Responses stream back through Chat Trigger automatically\n```\n\n**Validation will fail if**:\n- Chat Trigger has streaming but target is not AI Agent\n- AI Agent in streaming mode has main output connections\n\n### Pattern 2: Fallback Language Models\n\nFor production reliability with fallback language models:\n\n```typescript\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  operations: [\n    // Primary model\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "OpenAI GPT-4",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel",\n      targetIndex: 0\n    },\n    // Fallback model\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "Anthropic Claude",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel",\n      targetIndex: 1\n    }\n  ]\n})\n\n// Enable fallback on AI Agent\n{\n  type: "updateNode",\n  nodeName: "AI Agent",\n  updates: {\n    "parameters.needsFallback": true\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Pattern 3: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation)\n\nComplete knowledge base setup:\n\n```typescript\n// 1. Load documents\n{type: "addConnection", source: "PDF Loader", target: "Text Splitter", sourceOutput: "ai_document"}\n\n// 2. Split and embed\n{type: "addConnection", source: "Text Splitter", target: "Vector Store"}\n{type: "addConnection", source: "Embeddings", target: "Vector Store", sourceOutput: "ai_embedding"}\n\n// 3. Create search tool\n{type: "addConnection", source: "Vector Store", target: "Vector Store Tool", sourceOutput: "ai_vectorStore"}\n\n// 4. Give tool to agent\n{type: "addConnection", source: "Vector Store Tool", target: "AI Agent", sourceOutput: "ai_tool"}\n```\n\n### Pattern 4: Multi-Agent Systems\n\nSpecialized sub-agents for complex tasks:\n\n```typescript\n// Create sub-agents with specific expertise\n[\n  {name: "research_agent", description: "Deep research specialist"},\n  {name: "data_analyst", description: "Data analysis expert"},\n  {name: "writer_agent", description: "Content writing specialist"}\n].forEach(agent => {\n  // Add as AI Agent Tool to main coordinator agent\n  {\n    type: "addConnection",\n    source: agent.name,\n    target: "Coordinator Agent",\n    sourceOutput: "ai_tool"\n  }\n})\n```\n\n---\n\n## 6. Validation & Best Practices {#validation}\n\n### Always Validate Before Deployment\n\n```typescript\nconst result = n8n_validate_workflow({id: "workflow_id"})\n\nif (!result.valid) {\n  console.log("Errors:", result.errors)\n  console.log("Warnings:", result.warnings)\n  console.log("Suggestions:", result.suggestions)\n}\n```\n\n### Common Validation Errors\n\n1. **MISSING_LANGUAGE_MODEL**\n   - Problem: AI Agent has no ai_languageModel connection\n   - Fix: Connect a language model before creating AI Agent\n\n2. **MISSING_TOOL_DESCRIPTION**\n   - Problem: HTTP Request Tool has no toolDescription\n   - Fix: Add clear description (15+ characters)\n\n3. **STREAMING_WITH_MAIN_OUTPUT**\n   - Problem: AI Agent in streaming mode has outgoing main connections\n   - Fix: Remove main connections when using streaming\n\n4. **FALLBACK_MISSING_SECOND_MODEL**\n   - Problem: needsFallback=true but only 1 language model\n   - Fix: Add second language model or disable needsFallback\n\n### Best Practices Checklist\n\n✅ **Before Creating AI Agent**:\n- [ ] Language model is connected first\n- [ ] At least one tool is prepared (or will be added)\n- [ ] System message is thoughtful and specific\n\n✅ **For Each Tool**:\n- [ ] Has toolDescription/description (15+ characters)\n- [ ] toolDescription explains WHEN to use the tool\n- [ ] All required parameters are configured\n- [ ] Credentials are set up if needed\n\n✅ **For Production**:\n- [ ] Workflow validated with n8n_validate_workflow\n- [ ] Tested with real user queries\n- [ ] Fallback model configured for reliability\n- [ ] Error handling in place\n- [ ] maxIterations set appropriately (default 10, max 50)\n\n---\n\n## 7. Troubleshooting {#troubleshooting}\n\n### Problem: "AI Agent has no language model"\n\n**Cause**: Connection created AFTER AI Agent or using wrong sourceOutput\n\n**Solution**:\n```typescript\nn8n_update_partial_workflow({\n  operations: [\n    {\n      type: "addConnection",\n      source: "OpenAI Chat Model",\n      target: "AI Agent",\n      sourceOutput: "ai_languageModel"  // ← CRITICAL\n    }\n  ]\n})\n```\n\n### Problem: "Tool has no description"\n\n**Cause**: HTTP Request Tool or Code Tool missing toolDescription/description\n\n**Solution**:\n```typescript\n{\n  type: "updateNode",\n  nodeName: "HTTP Request Tool",\n  updates: {\n    "parameters.toolDescription": "Call weather API to get current conditions for a city"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Problem: "Streaming mode not working"\n\n**Causes**:\n1. Chat Trigger not set to streaming\n2. AI Agent has main output connections\n3. Target of Chat Trigger is not AI Agent\n\n**Solution**:\n```typescript\n// 1. Set Chat Trigger to streaming\n{\n  type: "updateNode",\n  nodeName: "Chat Trigger",\n  updates: {\n    "parameters.options.responseMode": "streaming"\n  }\n}\n\n// 2. Remove AI Agent main outputs\n{\n  type: "removeConnection",\n  source: "AI Agent",\n  target: "Any Output Node"\n}\n```\n\n### Problem: "Agent keeps looping"\n\n**Cause**: Tool not returning proper response or agent stuck in reasoning loop\n\n**Solutions**:\n1. Set maxIterations lower: `"parameters.maxIterations": 5`\n2. Improve tool descriptions to be more specific\n3. Add system message guidance: "Use tools efficiently, don't repeat actions"\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n### Essential Tools\n\n| Tool | Purpose | Key Parameters |\n|------|---------|----------------|\n| HTTP Request Tool | API calls | toolDescription, url, placeholders |\n| Code Tool | Custom logic | name, description, code, inputSchema |\n| Vector Store Tool | Knowledge search | description, topK |\n| AI Agent Tool | Sub-agents | name, description, systemMessage |\n| MCP Client Tool | MCP protocol | description, mcpServer, tool |\n\n### Connection Quick Codes\n\n```typescript\n// Language Model → AI Agent\nsourceOutput: "ai_languageModel"\n\n// Tool → AI Agent\nsourceOutput: "ai_tool"\n\n// Memory → AI Agent\nsourceOutput: "ai_memory"\n\n// Parser → AI Agent\nsourceOutput: "ai_outputParser"\n\n// Embeddings → Vector Store\nsourceOutput: "ai_embedding"\n\n// Vector Store → Vector Store Tool\nsourceOutput: "ai_vectorStore"\n```\n\n### Validation Command\n\n```typescript\nn8n_validate_workflow({id: "workflow_id"})\n```\n\n---\n\n## Related Resources\n\n- **FINAL_AI_VALIDATION_SPEC.md**: Complete validation rules\n- **n8n_update_partial_workflow**: Workflow modification tool\n- **search_nodes({query: "AI", includeExamples: true})**: Find AI nodes with examples\n- **get_node({nodeType: "...", detail: "standard", includeExamples: true})**: Node details with examples\n\n---\n\n*This guide is part of the n8n-mcp documentation system. For questions or issues, refer to the validation spec or use tools_documentation() for specific topics.*

# dryeab/mcp-telegram 653a1ed43c49 MIT
ok Send a message to a Telegram user, group, or channel.\n\nIt allows sending text messages to any Telegram entity identified by `entity`.\n\n!IMPORTANT: If you are not sure about the entity, use the `search_dialogs`\ntool and ask the user to select the correct entity from the list.\n\nArgs:\n    entity (`str`): The identifier of where to send the message.\n        This can be a Telegram chat ID, a username, a phone number\n        (in format '+1234567890'), or a group/channel username. The special\n        value "me" can be used to send a message to yourself.\n\n    message (`str`, optional): The text message to be sent.\n        The message supports Markdown formatting including **bold**, __italic__,\n        `monospace`, and [URL](links). The maximum length for a message is 35,000\n        bytes or 4,096 characters.\n\n    file_path (`list[str]`, optional): The list of paths to the files to be sent.\n\n    reply_to (`int`, optional): The message ID to reply to.\n\nReturns:\n    `str`:\n        A success message if sent, or an error message if failed.

# homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp 342e6b2e2de8 MIT
ok Manage the running ha-mcp server itself (developer mode).\n\nWhen NOT to use: to restart Home Assistant use ha_restart; to\nupdate Home Assistant Apps (add-ons) or HACS packages use\nha_manage_app / ha_manage_hacs.\n\nCaveats: update_source changes ONLY the ha_mcp_tools custom\ncomponent's separate in-process server entry — it never updates\nthe app (add-on), Docker, standalone, or PyPI server that may be\nserving this connection (update those via ha_manage_app /\ndocker pull / pip). In embedded mode that entry IS this server,\nso the update self-interrupts; elsewhere this connection is\nuntouched and keeps its current version. Success means the\nentry's options were applied — the component then reinstalls in\nthe background, which can take minutes and can still fail\n(check HA logs). update_source requires the component's\nin-process server entry to exist. restart interrupts this MCP\nconnection in embedded and app deployments (the reply\narrives just before the server goes down) and supports those\ntwo deployments only (standalone processes must be restarted\nexternally). approve/deny require the separate\n'dev_tools_security_policy_access' setting, off by default.\n\nEXAMPLES:\nha_dev_manage_server("update_source", pip_spec="https://github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp/archive/refs/pull/1234/head.tar.gz")\nha_dev_manage_server("update_source", pip_spec="clear")\nha_dev_manage_server("approve", token="abc123")
ok Create or update a dashboard resource (inline code or external URL).\n\nProvide exactly one of:\n- content: Inline JavaScript or CSS code (embedded in the resource URL\n  as a data: URI — no file storage or external hosting involved).\n  Supports 'module' and 'css' types only; URLs are\n  deterministic (same content = same URL); up to ~128KB. Content must be\n  self-contained: a data: URI has no base URL, so relative imports inside\n  a module and relative url() references inside CSS cannot resolve (use\n  fully-qualified URLs instead). If Home Assistant is behind a reverse\n  proxy that injects a Content-Security-Policy without 'data:' in\n  script-src/style-src, the browser blocks these resources: this call\n  still succeeds and the card simply never renders. Register the code as\n  a file and use url='/local/...' on such a deployment. (HA itself ships\n  no CSP.)\n- url: External resource URL — /local/... (files in /config/www/),\n  /hacsfiles/... (HACS-installed cards) or https://... (CDN). Supports\n  all types: 'module', 'js', 'css', 'html'.\n\nEXAMPLES:\n- Inline: ha_config_set_dashboard_resource(content="class MyCard extends HTMLElement { ... } customElements.define('my-card', MyCard);", resource_type="module")\n- HACS card (after ha_manage_hacs(action='download')): ha_config_set_dashboard_resource(url="/hacsfiles/lovelace-mushroom/mushroom.js", resource_type="module")\n- Update: ha_config_set_dashboard_resource(url="/local/my-card-v2.js", resource_type="module", resource_id="abc123")\n\nAfter adding a resource, a browser cache clear or hard refresh\n(Ctrl+Shift+R) is needed to load it.
ok Create or update a Home Assistant dashboard.\n\nMUST call ha_get_skill_guide OR refer to your locally installed skills first.\n`dashboard-guide.md` ships under `skill_content` by default. A card's\nfields: ha_config_get_dashboard(card_type=..., describe=True).\n\nMODES (pick one):\n- patch: edit known paths with literal values using JSON Patch\n  add/remove/replace/test and config_hash, e.g.\n  patch=[{"op": "replace", "path": "/views/0/title", "value": "Home"}].\n  move/copy are unsupported. Full guide:\n  https://github.com/homeassistant-ai/ha-mcp/blob/master/docs/dashboard-edits.md\n- python_transform: loops or pattern-based changes across cards and views,\n  e.g. 'config["views"][0]["cards"].append({"type": "button", "entity": "light.bedroom"})'.\n  After delete/add operations indices shift, so chain multiple ops in ONE\n  expression where possible; a later call needs a fresh config_hash from\n  ha_config_get_dashboard().\n- config: new dashboards only, or a full restructure. Replaces everything.\n  Omit it to create a dashboard without initial config.\n\nUse ha_config_get_dashboard(entity_id=...) to get the path of any card,\nand ha_search / ha_get_overview to find entity IDs — never guess them.\nFor visual re-checks after the write, use ha_get_dashboard_screenshot\n(when available) instead of re-sending config.\n\ntitle/icon/require_admin/show_in_sidebar can be updated in a\nmetadata-only call or alongside a full config replacement; with\npython_transform or patch, update metadata in a separate call (combining\nit with patch is rejected). Strategy dashboards (config\n{"strategy": {...}}) cannot be converted to custom dashboards here; use\n"Take Control" in the Home Assistant UI.\n\nEXAMPLE:\nha_config_set_dashboard(url_path="home-dashboard", title="Home Overview",\n    config={"views": [{"title": "Home", "type": "sections", "sections": [{"title": "Climate", "cards": [{"type": "tile", "entity": "climate.living_room"}]}]}]})\n\nThis tool manages storage-mode dashboards only. YAML-mode dashboards (a\n.yaml file registered under ``lovelace: dashboards:`` in\nconfiguration.yaml) and dashboards inlined under ``lovelace:`` are\nedited in their .yaml file; ``ha_config_set_yaml`` can update the\n``lovelace:`` registration but not the dashboard body.
ok Manage Home Assistant blueprints — list, read, import, save, delete, or render a standalone config.\n\nOne interface for the whole blueprint lifecycle in the ``automation``\nand ``script`` domains.\n\nDO NOT use this to create an automation or script FROM a blueprint —\nthat is ``ha_config_set_automation`` / ``ha_config_set_script`` with a\n``use_blueprint`` config.\n\nTo duplicate a blueprint, ``get`` it and ``save`` its ``yaml`` under a\nnew ``path``; to edit one in place, ``get`` it, change the text, and\n``save`` it back to the same ``path`` with ``overwrite=True``.\n\n``get`` also reports ``used_by``: the automations or scripts built on\nthe blueprint, which is the UI's "Show automations using this\nblueprint". Check it before deleting — Home Assistant refuses to delete a\nblueprint anything still uses (the error lists the consumers), and it\ngoes on counting a consumer that has since taken control of its own\nconfig until that consumer is removed.\n\nCAVEATS: ``get`` returns the on-disk YAML only when something can read\nit — an in-process server, the ha_mcp_tools component, the File & YAML\nTools entry, or the blueprint's ``source_url``; ``yaml_source`` names\nwhich one answered, and ``source_url`` text is a fresh download that can\ndiffer from the installed file. Core's blueprint API alone exposes\nmetadata only, so a locally authored blueprint on a bare install has no\nreadable text. Both writes are snapshotted first when a copy can be\nread, so ``ha_manage_backup(scope="edits")`` can restore the previous\nfile. ``substitute`` only renders — it writes nothing, so pass the\nreturned config to ``ha_config_set_automation`` /\n``ha_config_set_script`` to persist it. To convert an automation or\nscript that ALREADY exists, prefer those tools' ``take_control_of_blueprint=True``:\nit renders with that item's own current inputs and saves the result over\nitself in one call.\n\nEXAMPLES:\n- Get one (with its consumers in ``used_by``): ha_manage_blueprints(action="get", path="homeassistant/motion_light.yaml")\n- Import: ha_manage_blueprints(action="import", url="https://example.com/bp.yaml")\n- Edit in place: ha_manage_blueprints(action="save", path="user/motion.yaml", yaml=<edited text>, overwrite=True)\n- Delete: ha_manage_blueprints(action="delete", path="user/motion.yaml", confirm=True)\n- Render standalone: ha_manage_blueprints(action="substitute", path="user/motion.yaml", input={"motion_sensor": "binary_sensor.hall"})\n\nRELATED TOOLS: ``ha_config_remove_automation`` / ``ha_config_remove_script``\nto clear consumers blocking a delete, ``ha_search`` to find them.
ok Run an MCP server or connect to a remote one.\n\nThe server can be specified in several ways:\n1. Module approach: "server.py" - runs the module directly, looking for an object named 'mcp', 'server', or 'app'\n2. Import approach: "server.py:app" - imports and runs the specified server object\n3. URL approach: "http://server-url" - connects to a remote server and creates a proxy\n4. MCPConfig file: "mcp.json" - runs as a proxy server for the MCP Servers in the MCPConfig file\n5. FastMCP config: "fastmcp.json" - runs server using FastMCP configuration\n6. No argument: looks for fastmcp.json in current directory\n7. Module mode: "-m my_module" - runs the module directly via python -m\n\nServer arguments can be passed after -- :\nfastmcp run server.py -- --config config.json --debug\n\nArgs:\n    server_spec: Python file, object specification (file:obj), config file, URL, or None to auto-detect
ok State of the WebSocket connection.\n\nDefined in 4.1_, 4.2_, 7.1.3_, and 7.1.4_ of :rfc:`6455`.\n\n.. _4.1: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-4.1\n.. _4.2: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-4.2\n.. _7.1.3: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-7.1.3\n.. _7.1.4: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-7.1.4
ok WebSocket close reason  received from the remote endpoint.\n\nDefined in 7.1.6_ of :rfc:`6455`.\n\n.. _7.1.6: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-7.1.6\n\n:obj:`None` if the connection isn't closed yet.
ok Receive the next message.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`recv` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal closure\nand :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure. This is how you detect the end of the\nmessage stream.\n\nCanceling :meth:`recv` is safe. There's no risk of losing data. The next\ninvocation of :meth:`recv` will return the next message.\n\nThis makes it possible to enforce a timeout by wrapping :meth:`recv` in\n:func:`~trio.move_on_after` or :func:`~trio.fail_after`.\n\nWhen the message is fragmented, :meth:`recv` waits until all fragments\nare received, reassembles them, and returns the whole message.\n\nArgs:\n    decode: Set this flag to override the default behavior of returning\n        :class:`str` or :class:`bytes`. See below for details.\n\nReturns:\n    A string (:class:`str`) for a Text_ frame or a bytestring\n    (:class:`bytes`) for a Binary_ frame.\n\n    .. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n    .. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\n    You may override this behavior with the ``decode`` argument:\n\n    * Set ``decode=False`` to disable UTF-8 decoding of Text_ frames and\n      return a bytestring (:class:`bytes`). This improves performance\n      when decoding isn't needed, for example if the message contains\n      JSON and you're using a JSON library that expects a bytestring.\n    * Set ``decode=True`` to force UTF-8 decoding of Binary_ frames\n      and return a string (:class:`str`). This may be useful for\n      servers that send binary frames instead of text frames.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    ConcurrencyError: If two coroutines call :meth:`recv` or\n        :meth:`recv_streaming` concurrently.
ok Send a message.\n\nA string (:class:`str`) is sent as a Text_ frame. A bytestring or\nbytes-like object (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or\n:class:`memoryview`) is sent as a Binary_ frame.\n\n.. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n.. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\nYou may override this behavior with the ``text`` argument:\n\n* Set ``text=True`` to send an UTF-8 bytestring or bytes-like object\n  (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or :class:`memoryview`) in a\n  Text_ frame. This improves performance when the message is already\n  UTF-8 encoded, for example if the message contains JSON and you're\n  using a JSON library that produces a bytestring.\n* Set ``text=False`` to send a string (:class:`str`) in a Binary_\n  frame. This may be useful for servers that expect binary frames\n  instead of text frames.\n\n:meth:`send` also accepts an iterable or asynchronous iterable of\nstrings, bytestrings, or bytes-like objects to enable fragmentation_.\nEach item is treated as a message fragment and sent in its own frame.\nAll items must be of the same type, or else :meth:`send` will raise a\n:exc:`TypeError` and the connection will be closed.\n\n.. _fragmentation: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.4\n\n:meth:`send` rejects dict-like objects because this is often an error.\n(If you really want to send the keys of a dict-like object as fragments,\ncall its :meth:`~dict.keys` method and pass the result to :meth:`send`.)\n\nCanceling :meth:`send` is discouraged. Instead, you should close the\nconnection with :meth:`aclose`. Indeed, there are only two situations\nwhere :meth:`send` may yield control to the event loop and then get\ncanceled; in both cases, :meth:`aclose` has the same effect and is\nmore clear:\n\n1. The write buffer is full. If you don't want to wait until enough\n   data is sent, your only alternative is to close the connection.\n   :meth:`aclose` will likely time out then abort the TCP connection.\n2. ``message`` is an asynchronous iterator that yields control.\n   Stopping in the middle of a fragmented message will cause a\n   protocol error and the connection will be closed.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`send` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it\nraises :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal\nconnection closure and\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure.\n\nArgs:\n    message: Message to send.\n    text: Force sending in a Text_ or Binary_ frame.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    TypeError: If ``message`` doesn't have a supported type.
ok Create a WebSocket server dispatching connections to different handlers.\n\nThis feature requires the third-party library `werkzeug`_:\n\n.. code-block:: console\n\n    $ pip install werkzeug\n\n.. _werkzeug: https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/\n\n:func:`route` accepts the same arguments as\n:func:`~websockets.trio.server.serve`, except as described below.\n\nThe first argument is a :class:`werkzeug.routing.Map` that maps URL patterns\nto connection handlers. In addition to the connection, handlers receive\nparameters captured in the URL as keyword arguments.\n\nHere's an example::\n\n    from websockets.trio.router import route\n    from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule\n\n    async def channel_handler(websocket, channel_id):\n        ...\n\n    url_map = Map([\n        Rule("/channel/<uuid:channel_id>", endpoint=channel_handler),\n        ...\n    ])\n\n    # set this event to exit the server\n    stop = trio.Event()\n\n    with trio.open_nursery() as nursery:\n        server = await nursery.start(route, url_map, ...)\n        async with server:\n            await stop.wait()\n\nRefer to the documentation of :mod:`werkzeug.routing` for details.\n\nIf you define redirects with ``Rule(..., redirect_to=...)`` in the URL map,\nwhen the server runs behind a reverse proxy that modifies the ``Host``\nheader or terminates TLS, you need additional configuration:\n\n* Set ``server_name`` to the name of the server as seen by clients. When\n  not provided, websockets uses the value of the ``Host`` header.\n\n* Set ``ssl=True`` to generate ``wss://`` URIs without enabling TLS.\n  Under the hood, this bind the URL map with a ``url_scheme`` of\n  ``wss://`` instead of ``ws://``.\n\nThere is no need to specify ``websocket=True`` in each rule. It is added\nautomatically.\n\nArgs:\n    url_map: Mapping of URL patterns to connection handlers.\n    server_name: Name of the server as seen by clients. If :obj:`None`,\n        websockets uses the value of the ``Host`` header.\n    ssl: Configuration for enabling TLS on the connection. Set it to\n        :obj:`True` if a reverse proxy terminates TLS connections.\n    create_router: Factory for the :class:`Router` dispatching requests to\n        handlers. Set it to a wrapper or a subclass to customize routing.\n    task_status: For compatibility with :meth:`nursery.start\n        <trio.Nursery.start>`.
ok WebSocket close reason, defined in `section 7.1.6 of RFC 6455`_.\n\n.. _section 7.1.6 of RFC 6455:\n    https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-7.1.6\n\n:obj:`None` if the connection isn't closed yet.
ok Receive the next message.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`recv` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal\nconnection closure and\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure. This is how you detect the end of the\nmessage stream.\n\nCanceling :meth:`recv` is safe. There's no risk of losing the next\nmessage. The next invocation of :meth:`recv` will return it.\n\nThis makes it possible to enforce a timeout by wrapping :meth:`recv` in\n:func:`~asyncio.timeout` or :func:`~asyncio.wait_for`.\n\nReturns:\n    A string (:class:`str`) for a Text_ frame. A bytestring\n    (:class:`bytes`) for a Binary_ frame.\n\n    .. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n    .. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    RuntimeError: If two coroutines call :meth:`recv` concurrently.
ok Send a message.\n\nA string (:class:`str`) is sent as a Text_ frame. A bytestring or\nbytes-like object (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or\n:class:`memoryview`) is sent as a Binary_ frame.\n\n.. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n.. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\n:meth:`send` also accepts an iterable or an asynchronous iterable of\nstrings, bytestrings, or bytes-like objects to enable fragmentation_.\nEach item is treated as a message fragment and sent in its own frame.\nAll items must be of the same type, or else :meth:`send` will raise a\n:exc:`TypeError` and the connection will be closed.\n\n.. _fragmentation: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.4\n\n:meth:`send` rejects dict-like objects because this is often an error.\n(If you want to send the keys of a dict-like object as fragments, call\nits :meth:`~dict.keys` method and pass the result to :meth:`send`.)\n\nCanceling :meth:`send` is discouraged. Instead, you should close the\nconnection with :meth:`close`. Indeed, there are only two situations\nwhere :meth:`send` may yield control to the event loop and then get\ncanceled; in both cases, :meth:`close` has the same effect and is\nmore clear:\n\n1. The write buffer is full. If you don't want to wait until enough\n   data is sent, your only alternative is to close the connection.\n   :meth:`close` will likely time out then abort the TCP connection.\n2. ``message`` is an asynchronous iterator that yields control.\n   Stopping in the middle of a fragmented message will cause a\n   protocol error and the connection will be closed.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`send` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it\nraises :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal\nconnection closure and\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure.\n\nArgs:\n    message: Message to send.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    TypeError: If ``message`` doesn't have a supported type.
ok Receive the next message.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`recv` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal closure\nand :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure. This is how you detect the end of the\nmessage stream.\n\nIf ``timeout`` is :obj:`None`, block until a message is received. If\n``timeout`` is set, wait up to ``timeout`` seconds for a message to be\nreceived and return it, else raise :exc:`TimeoutError`. If ``timeout``\nis ``0`` or negative, check if a message has been received already and\nreturn it, else raise :exc:`TimeoutError`.\n\nWhen the message is fragmented, :meth:`recv` waits until all fragments\nare received, reassembles them, and returns the whole message.\n\nArgs:\n    timeout: Timeout for receiving a message in seconds.\n    decode: Set this flag to override the default behavior of returning\n        :class:`str` or :class:`bytes`. See below for details.\n\nReturns:\n    A string (:class:`str`) for a Text_ frame or a bytestring\n    (:class:`bytes`) for a Binary_ frame.\n\n    .. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n    .. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\n    You may override this behavior with the ``decode`` argument:\n\n    * Set ``decode=False`` to disable UTF-8 decoding of Text_ frames and\n      return a bytestring (:class:`bytes`). This improves performance\n      when decoding isn't needed, for example if the message contains\n      JSON and you're using a JSON library that expects a bytestring.\n    * Set ``decode=True`` to force UTF-8 decoding of Binary_ frames and\n      return strings (:class:`str`). This may be useful for servers that\n      send binary frames instead of text frames.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    ConcurrencyError: If two threads call :meth:`recv` or\n        :meth:`recv_streaming` concurrently.
ok Send a message.\n\nA string (:class:`str`) is sent as a Text_ frame. A bytestring or\nbytes-like object (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or\n:class:`memoryview`) is sent as a Binary_ frame.\n\n.. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n.. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\nYou may override this behavior with the ``text`` argument:\n\n* Set ``text=True`` to send an UTF-8 bytestring or bytes-like object\n  (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or :class:`memoryview`) in a\n  Text_ frame. This improves performance when the message is already\n  UTF-8 encoded, for example if the message contains JSON and you're\n  using a JSON library that produces a bytestring.\n* Set ``text=False`` to send a string (:class:`str`) in a Binary_\n  frame. This may be useful for servers that expect binary frames\n  instead of text frames.\n\n:meth:`send` also accepts an iterable of strings, bytestrings, or\nbytes-like objects to enable fragmentation_. Each item is treated as a\nmessage fragment and sent in its own frame. All items must be of the\nsame type, or else :meth:`send` will raise a :exc:`TypeError` and the\nconnection will be closed.\n\n.. _fragmentation: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.4\n\n:meth:`send` rejects dict-like objects because this is often an error.\n(If you really want to send the keys of a dict-like object as fragments,\ncall its :meth:`~dict.keys` method and pass the result to :meth:`send`.)\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`send` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it\nraises :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal\nconnection closure and\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure.\n\nArgs:\n    message: Message to send.\n    text: Force sending in a Text_ or Binary_ frame.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    ConcurrencyError: If the connection is sending a fragmented message.\n    TypeError: If ``message`` doesn't have a supported type.
ok Create a WebSocket server dispatching connections to different handlers.\n\nThis feature requires the third-party library `werkzeug`_:\n\n.. code-block:: console\n\n    $ pip install werkzeug\n\n.. _werkzeug: https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/\n\n:func:`route` accepts the same arguments as\n:func:`~websockets.sync.server.serve`, except as described below.\n\nThe first argument is a :class:`werkzeug.routing.Map` that maps URL patterns\nto connection handlers. In addition to the connection, handlers receive\nparameters captured in the URL as keyword arguments.\n\nHere's an example::\n\n\n    from websockets.sync.router import route\n    from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule\n\n    def channel_handler(websocket, channel_id):\n        ...\n\n    url_map = Map([\n        Rule("/channel/<uuid:channel_id>", endpoint=channel_handler),\n        ...\n    ])\n\n    with route(url_map, ...) as server:\n        server.serve_forever()\n\nRefer to the documentation of :mod:`werkzeug.routing` for details.\n\nIf you define redirects with ``Rule(..., redirect_to=...)`` in the URL map,\nwhen the server runs behind a reverse proxy that modifies the ``Host``\nheader or terminates TLS, you need additional configuration:\n\n* Set ``server_name`` to the name of the server as seen by clients. When\n  not provided, websockets uses the value of the ``Host`` header.\n\n* Set ``ssl=True`` to generate ``wss://`` URIs without enabling TLS.\n  Under the hood, this bind the URL map with a ``url_scheme`` of\n  ``wss://`` instead of ``ws://``.\n\nThere is no need to specify ``websocket=True`` in each rule. It is added\nautomatically.\n\nArgs:\n    url_map: Mapping of URL patterns to connection handlers.\n    server_name: Name of the server as seen by clients. If :obj:`None`,\n        websockets uses the value of the ``Host`` header.\n    ssl: Configuration for enabling TLS on the connection. Set it to\n        :obj:`True` if a reverse proxy terminates TLS connections.\n    create_router: Factory for the :class:`Router` dispatching requests to\n        handlers. Set it to a wrapper or a subclass to customize routing.
ok Receive the next message.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`recv` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal closure\nand :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure. This is how you detect the end of the\nmessage stream.\n\nCanceling :meth:`recv` is safe. There's no risk of losing data. The next\ninvocation of :meth:`recv` will return the next message.\n\nThis makes it possible to enforce a timeout by wrapping :meth:`recv` in\n:func:`~asyncio.timeout` or :func:`~asyncio.wait_for`.\n\nWhen the message is fragmented, :meth:`recv` waits until all fragments\nare received, reassembles them, and returns the whole message.\n\nArgs:\n    decode: Set this flag to override the default behavior of returning\n        :class:`str` or :class:`bytes`. See below for details.\n\nReturns:\n    A string (:class:`str`) for a Text_ frame or a bytestring\n    (:class:`bytes`) for a Binary_ frame.\n\n    .. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n    .. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\n    You may override this behavior with the ``decode`` argument:\n\n    * Set ``decode=False`` to disable UTF-8 decoding of Text_ frames and\n      return a bytestring (:class:`bytes`). This improves performance\n      when decoding isn't needed, for example if the message contains\n      JSON and you're using a JSON library that expects a bytestring.\n    * Set ``decode=True`` to force UTF-8 decoding of Binary_ frames and\n      return strings (:class:`str`). This may be useful for servers that\n      send binary frames instead of text frames.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    ConcurrencyError: If two coroutines call :meth:`recv` or\n        :meth:`recv_streaming` concurrently.
ok Send a message.\n\nA string (:class:`str`) is sent as a Text_ frame. A bytestring or\nbytes-like object (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or\n:class:`memoryview`) is sent as a Binary_ frame.\n\n.. _Text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n.. _Binary: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.6\n\nYou may override this behavior with the ``text`` argument:\n\n* Set ``text=True`` to send an UTF-8 bytestring or bytes-like object\n  (:class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray`, or :class:`memoryview`) in a\n  Text_ frame. This improves performance when the message is already\n  UTF-8 encoded, for example if the message contains JSON and you're\n  using a JSON library that produces a bytestring.\n* Set ``text=False`` to send a string (:class:`str`) in a Binary_\n  frame. This may be useful for servers that expect binary frames\n  instead of text frames.\n\n:meth:`send` also accepts an iterable or asynchronous iterable of\nstrings, bytestrings, or bytes-like objects to enable fragmentation_.\nEach item is treated as a message fragment and sent in its own frame.\nAll items must be of the same type, or else :meth:`send` will raise a\n:exc:`TypeError` and the connection will be closed.\n\n.. _fragmentation: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6455#section-5.4\n\n:meth:`send` rejects dict-like objects because this is often an error.\n(If you really want to send the keys of a dict-like object as fragments,\ncall its :meth:`~dict.keys` method and pass the result to :meth:`send`.)\n\nCanceling :meth:`send` is discouraged. Instead, you should close the\nconnection with :meth:`close`. Indeed, there are only two situations\nwhere :meth:`send` may yield control to the event loop and then get\ncanceled; in both cases, :meth:`close` has the same effect and the\neffect is more obvious:\n\n1. The write buffer is full. If you don't want to wait until enough\n   data is sent, your only alternative is to close the connection.\n   :meth:`close` will likely time out then abort the TCP connection.\n2. ``message`` is an asynchronous iterator that yields control.\n   Stopping in the middle of a fragmented message will cause a\n   protocol error and the connection will be closed.\n\nWhen the connection is closed, :meth:`send` raises\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed`. Specifically, it\nraises :exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedOK` after a normal\nconnection closure and\n:exc:`~websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosedError` after a protocol\nerror or a network failure.\n\nArgs:\n    message: Message to send.\n    text: Force sending in a Text_ or Binary_ frame.\n\nRaises:\n    ConnectionClosed: When the connection is closed.\n    TypeError: If ``message`` doesn't have a supported type.
ok Create a WebSocket server dispatching connections to different handlers.\n\nThis feature requires the third-party library `werkzeug`_:\n\n.. code-block:: console\n\n    $ pip install werkzeug\n\n.. _werkzeug: https://werkzeug.palletsprojects.com/\n\n:func:`route` accepts the same arguments as\n:func:`~websockets.sync.server.serve`, except as described below.\n\nThe first argument is a :class:`werkzeug.routing.Map` that maps URL patterns\nto connection handlers. In addition to the connection, handlers receive\nparameters captured in the URL as keyword arguments.\n\nHere's an example::\n\n    from websockets.asyncio.router import route\n    from werkzeug.routing import Map, Rule\n\n    async def channel_handler(websocket, channel_id):\n        ...\n\n    url_map = Map([\n        Rule("/channel/<uuid:channel_id>", endpoint=channel_handler),\n        ...\n    ])\n\n    # set this event to exit the server\n    stop = asyncio.Event()\n\n    async with route(url_map, ...) as server:\n        await stop.wait()\n\nRefer to the documentation of :mod:`werkzeug.routing` for details.\n\nIf you define redirects with ``Rule(..., redirect_to=...)`` in the URL map,\nwhen the server runs behind a reverse proxy that modifies the ``Host``\nheader or terminates TLS, you need additional configuration:\n\n* Set ``server_name`` to the name of the server as seen by clients. When\n  not provided, websockets uses the value of the ``Host`` header.\n\n* Set ``ssl=True`` to generate ``wss://`` URIs without enabling TLS.\n  Under the hood, this bind the URL map with a ``url_scheme`` of\n  ``wss://`` instead of ``ws://``.\n\nThere is no need to specify ``websocket=True`` in each rule. It is added\nautomatically.\n\nLike :func:`~websockets.sync.server.serve`, :func:`route` returns a\n:class:`~websockets.sync.server.Server` that you can also run with\n:meth:`~websockets.sync.server.Server.serve_forever`.\n\nArgs:\n    url_map: Mapping of URL patterns to connection handlers.\n    server_name: Name of the server as seen by clients. If :obj:`None`,\n        websockets uses the value of the ``Host`` header.\n    ssl: Configuration for enabling TLS on the connection. Set it to\n        :obj:`True` if a reverse proxy terminates TLS connections.\n    create_router: Factory for the :class:`Router` dispatching requests to\n        handlers. Set it to a wrapper or a subclass to customize routing.

ok Manages calendar events. Supports creating, updating, deleting, and RSVP.\n\nArgs:\n    user_google_email (str): The user's Google email address. Required.\n    action (str): Action to perform - "create", "update", "delete", or "rsvp".\n    summary (Optional[str]): Event title (required for create).\n    start_time (Optional[str]): Start time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply start_timezone or timezone. For a local wall-clock time, omit the offset and pass the zone so Google resolves daylight saving; a wrong offset moves the event. Date-only values create all-day events.\n    end_time (Optional[str]): End time (required for create). An RFC3339 UTC offset identifies the exact instant and is preserved. Without an offset, supply end_timezone or timezone. All-day end dates are exclusive.\n    event_id (Optional[str]): Event ID (required for update and delete).\n    calendar_id (str): Calendar ID (default: 'primary').\n    description (Optional[str]): Event description.\n    location (Optional[str]): Event location.\n    attendees (Optional[List[Union[str, Dict[str, Any]]]]): Attendee email addresses, attendee objects (e.g. {"email": ..., "responseStatus": "accepted"}), or a mix of both.\n    timezone (Optional[str]): IANA timezone applied to both boundaries (e.g.,\n        "America/New_York"). Converts offset-bearing timestamps without changing their\n        instant; interprets offset-free timestamps as local times in this zone.\n        Overridden per boundary by start_timezone/end_timezone.\n    start_timezone (Optional[str]): IANA timezone for the start boundary only,\n        overriding timezone. Use for events whose two ends sit in different zones -\n        a flight departing 13:45 "Asia/Jerusalem" and landing 17:50\n        "Europe/Amsterdam" is one event authored in two zones. Explicit timestamp\n        offsets always preserve the instant, even when the zone differs.\n    end_timezone (Optional[str]): IANA timezone for the end boundary only,\n        overriding timezone. ok Modifies values in a specific range of a Google Sheet - can write, update, or clear values,\nor insert Smart Chips (Drive files/folders or People).\n\nArgs:\n    user_google_email (str): The user's Google email address. Required.\n    spreadsheet_id (str): The ID of the spreadsheet. Required.\n    range_name (str): The range to modify (e.g., "Sheet1!A1:D10", "A1:D10"). Required.\n    values (Optional[Union[str, List[List[str]]]]): 2D array of values to write/update. Can be a JSON string or Python list. Required unless clear_values=True or chips is provided.\n    value_input_option (str): How to interpret input values ("RAW" or "USER_ENTERED"). Defaults to "USER_ENTERED".\n    clear_values (bool): If True, clears the range instead of writing values. Defaults to False.\n    chips (Optional[Union[str, dict, List[Any]]]): Smart chip(s) to insert instead of values:\n        - A single URL or email string for a single cell (e.g., "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/123", "user@example.com").\n        - A list of URLs or emails for a single cell (multiple chips) or across cells (e.g., ["https://...", "https://..."]).\n        - A 2D list of URLs/emails matching a grid range. For a single-row or single-column\n          range, each inner list is instead the chips for one cell (e.g., [["a@x.com", "b@x.com"]]\n          puts both chips in the first cell of "A1:C1").\n        - A dict or list of dicts with explicit properties (e.g., {"type": "drive", "uri": "..."}, {"type": "person", "email": "..."}).\n        - A JSON-encoded string representing any of the above formats.\n    chip_type (Optional[str]): Explicit chip type if passing raw strings in chips: "drive" (default for URLs/IDs) or "person" (default for emails).\n\nReturns:\n    str: Confirmation message of the successful modification operation.
ok Sends an email using the user's Gmail account. Supports new emails, replies, and\nforwards, with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to send\nfrom configured alias addresses.\n\nTo forward an existing message, pass forward_message_id. The original subject,\nbody (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are carried over.\nIn forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note and subject is optional.\nThreading, reply, and signature options do not apply when forwarding.\n\nTHIS TOOL SENDS IMMEDIATELY AND CANNOT SCHEDULE. Gmail's REST API exposes no\nsend-time parameter; Schedule send is a web-UI feature with no API equivalent,\nso no argument to this tool can defer delivery. Never tell a user a message\nwas scheduled. For "prepare now, deliver later", create a draft with\ndraft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to\ncreate and send a new message via send_gmail_message at the chosen time, or\ncall users.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.\nAlternatively, let the user schedule that draft in the Gmail UI.\n\nArgs:\n    to (str): Recipient email address.\n    subject (str): Email subject. Required for a new message. Optional when replying\n        with thread_id (inherits the parent message's subject) or forwarding (then\n        defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').\n    body (str): Email body content. Required unless forwarding (then an optional prepended note).\n    body_format (Literal['plain', 'html']): Body format (and prepended note format when forwarding). Defaults to 'plain'.\n    forward_message_id (Optional[str]): Gmail message ID to forward. When set, the tool forwards that message.\n    include_forwarded_attachments (bool): Whether to carry over the original attachments when forwarding. Defaults to True.\n    attachments (Optional[List[Dict[str, str]]]): Optional list of attachments. Each dict can contain:\n        Option 1 - File path (auto-encodes):\n          - 'path' (required): File path to attach\n          - 'filename' (optional): Override filename\n          - 'mime_type' (optional): Override MIME type (auto-detected if not provided)\n        Option 2 - Base64 content:\n          - 'content' (required): Standard base64-encoded file content (not urlsafe)\n          - 'filename' (required): Name of the file\n          - 'mime_type' (optional): MIME type (defaults to 'application/octet-stream')\n    cc (Optional[str]): Optional CC email address.\n    bcc (Optional[str]): Optional BCC email address.\n    from_name (Optional[str]): Optional sender display name. If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.\n    from_email (Optional[str]): Optional 'Send As' alias email address. The alias must be\n        configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided,\n        the email will be sent from the authenticated user's primary email address.\n    user_google_email (str): The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.\n    thread_id (Optional[str]): Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When\n        in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message\n        with an RFC Message-ID.\n    in_reply_to (Optional[str]): Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to\n        a specific message. Omit to reply to the latest eligible message.\n    references (Optional[str]): Optional RFC Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally\n        omit when thread_id is provided; the chain is derived automatically.\n    include_signature (bool): Whether to append Gmail signature HTML from send-as settings.\n        When include_signature is true and Gmail signature retrieval fails for benign reasons\n        (e.g., missing gmail.settings.basic scope), the send proceeds without a signature.\n        Non-benign failures such as quota/rate-limit or API errors raise ToolError and abort\n        the send.\n    quote_original (bool): Whether to append the message being replied to as a quoted\n        original. Only has an effect when thread_id is provided.\n    reply_all (bool): Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the\n        sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated\n        account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win over the derived\n        values; when cc is omitted, the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc\n        unless they are already in To (so an explicit 'to' that redirects the reply still\n        keeps them on it).\n\nReturns:\n    str: Confirmation message with the sent email's message ID.\n\nExamples:\n    # Send a new email\n    send_gmail_message(to="user@example.com", subject="Hello", body="Hi there!")\n\n    # Send with a custom display name\n    send_gmail_message(to="user@example.com", subject="Hello", body="Hi there!", from_name="John Doe")\n\n    # Send an HTML email\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        subject="Hello",\n        body="<strong>Hi there!</strong>",\n        body_format="html"\n    )\n\n    # Send from a configured alias (Send As)\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        subject="Business Inquiry",\n        body="Hello from my business address...",\n        from_email="business@mydomain.com"\n    )\n\n    # Send an email with CC and BCC\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        cc="manager@example.com",\n        bcc="archive@example.com",\n        subject="Project Update",\n        body="Here's the latest update..."\n    )\n\n    # Send an email with attachments (using file path)\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        subject="Report",\n        body="Please see attached report.",\n        attachments=[{\n            "path": "/path/to/report.pdf"\n        }]\n    )\n\n    # Send an email with attachments (using base64 content)\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        subject="Report",\n        body="Please see attached report.",\n        attachments=[{\n            "filename": "report.pdf",\n            "content": "JVBERi0xLjQK...",  # base64 encoded PDF\n            "mime_type": "application/pdf"\n        }]\n    )\n\n    # Send a reply\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        subject="Re: Meeting tomorrow",\n        body="Thanks for the update!",\n        thread_id="thread_123"\n    )\n\n    # Send a reply-all with the original quoted, deriving headers and\n    # recipients from the thread\n    send_gmail_message(\n        subject="Re: Meeting tomorrow",\n        body="Thanks for the update!",\n        thread_id="thread_123",\n        reply_all=True,\n        quote_original=True\n    )\n\n    # Forward a message with a note\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        forward_message_id="abc123",\n        body="FYI - see below."\n    )\n\n    # Forward without the original attachments\n    send_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        forward_message_id="abc123",\n        include_forwarded_attachments=False\n    )
ok Creates a draft email in the user's Gmail account. Supports new, reply, and forward\ndrafts with optional attachments. Supports Gmail's "Send As" feature to draft from\nconfigured alias addresses.\n\nTo save a forward as a draft for review, pass forward_message_id. The original\nsubject, body (quoted with a "Forwarded message" header), and attachments are\ncarried over. In forward mode, body (if any) is prepended as a note, subject is\noptional, and threading, reply, and signature options do not apply.\n\nSCHEDULED SEND IS NOT AVAILABLE. Gmail's REST API exposes no send-time\nparameter; the Schedule send feature is web-UI only, and a message cannot be\nplaced in the Scheduled folder through the API. Do not claim a message was\nscheduled. To deliver at a chosen time, create a draft with\ndraft_gmail_message. An external scheduler must retain the message data to\ncreate and send a new message via send_gmail_message then, or call\nusers.drafts.send with the draft ID returned by draft_gmail_message.\nAlternatively, let the user schedule the draft in the Gmail UI.\n\nArgs:\n    user_google_email (str): The user's Google email address. Required for authentication.\n    subject (Optional[str]): Email subject. Required for a new draft. Optional when\n        replying with thread_id (inherits the parent message's subject) or forwarding\n        (then defaults to 'Fwd: <original subject>').\n    body (Optional[str]): Email body. Required unless forwarding (then an optional prepended note).\n    body_format (Literal['plain', 'html']): Email body format. Defaults to 'plain'.\n    forward_message_id (Optional[str]): Gmail message ID to forward. When set, the draft is a forward of that message.\n    include_forwarded_attachments (bool): Whether to carry over the original attachments when forwarding. Defaults to True.\n    to (Optional[str]): Optional recipient email address. Can be left empty for drafts.\n    cc (Optional[str]): Optional CC email address.\n    bcc (Optional[str]): Optional BCC email address.\n    from_name (Optional[str]): Optional sender display name. If provided, the From header will be formatted as 'Name <email>'.\n    from_email (Optional[str]): Optional 'Send As' alias email address. The alias must be\n        configured in Gmail settings (Settings > Accounts > Send mail as). If not provided,\n        the draft uses the account's default Send As address, then the primary or first\n        usable Send-As entry, falling back to the authenticated user's email when Gmail\n        returns no usable entry or settings access is not authorized.\n    thread_id (Optional[str]): Optional Gmail thread ID to reply within. When\n        in_reply_to is omitted, replies to the latest non-draft, non-trash message\n        with an RFC Message-ID.\n    in_reply_to (Optional[str]): Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to\n        a specific message. Omit to reply to the latest eligible message.\n    references (Optional[str]): Optional RFC Message-ID ancestry chain. Normally\n        omit when thread_id is provided; the chain is derived automatically.\n    attachments (List[Dict[str, str]]): Optional list of attachments. Each dict can contain:\n        Option 1 - File path (auto-encodes):\n          - 'path' (required): File path to attach\n          - 'filename' (optional): Override filename\n          - 'mime_type' (optional): Override MIME type (auto-detected if not provided)\n        Option 2 - Base64 content:\n          - 'content' (required): Standard base64-encoded file content (not urlsafe)\n          - 'filename' (required): Name of the file\n          - 'mime_type' (optional): MIME type (defaults to 'application/octet-stream')\n    include_signature (bool): Whether to append Gmail signature HTML from send-as settings.\n        When include_signature is true and Gmail signature retrieval fails for benign reasons\n        (e.g., missing settings authorization), the draft proceeds with the requested or\n        authenticated sender and without a signature.\n        Non-benign failures such as quota/rate-limit or API errors raise ToolError and abort\n        the draft.\n    quote_original (bool): Whether to include the original message as a quoted reply.\n        Only has an effect when thread_id is provided. When enabled, fetches the\n        original message and appends it below the signature. Defaults to False.\n    reply_all (bool): Whether to derive reply-all recipients from the thread: To = the\n        sender being replied to, Cc = the other participants, excluding the authenticated\n        account and from_email. Requires thread_id. Explicit to/cc win over the derived\n        values; when cc is omitted, the sender being replied to is added to the derived Cc\n        unless they are already in To.\n\nReturns:\n    str: Confirmation message with the created draft's ID.\n\nExamples:\n    # Create a new draft\n    draft_gmail_message(subject="Hello", body="Hi there!", to="user@example.com")\n\n    # Create a draft from a configured alias (Send As)\n    draft_gmail_message(\n        subject="Business Inquiry",\n        body="Hello from my business address...",\n        to="user@example.com",\n        from_email="business@mydomain.com"\n    )\n\n    # Create a plaintext draft with CC and BCC\n    draft_gmail_message(\n        subject="Project Update",\n        body="Here's the latest update...",\n        to="user@example.com",\n        cc="manager@example.com",\n        bcc="archive@example.com"\n    )\n\n    # Create a HTML draft with CC and BCC\n    draft_gmail_message(\n        subject="Project Update",\n        body="<strong>Hi there!</strong>",\n        body_format="html",\n        to="user@example.com",\n        cc="manager@example.com",\n        bcc="archive@example.com"\n    )\n\n    # Create a reply draft in plaintext\n    draft_gmail_message(\n        subject="Re: Meeting tomorrow",\n        body="Thanks for the update!",\n        to="user@example.com",\n        thread_id="thread_123"\n    )\n\n    # Create a reply draft in HTML\n    draft_gmail_message(\n        subject="Re: Meeting tomorrow",\n        body="<strong>Thanks for the update!</strong>",\n        body_format="html",\n        to="user@example.com",\n        thread_id="thread_123"\n    )\n\n    # Save a forward (with the original attachments) as a draft for review\n    draft_gmail_message(\n        to="user@example.com",\n        forward_message_id="abc123",\n        body="FYI - see below."\n    )

ok Search query - can be either a simple text (e.g. 'project documentation') or a CQL query string. Simple queries use 'siteSearch' by default, to mimic the WebUI search, with an automatic fallback to 'text' search if not supported. Examples of CQL:\n- Basic search: 'type=page AND space=DEV'\n- Personal space search: 'space="~username"' (note: personal space keys starting with ~ must be quoted)\n- Search by title: 'title~"Meeting Notes"'\n- Use siteSearch: 'siteSearch ~ "important concept"'\n- Use text search: 'text ~ "important concept"'\n- Recent content: 'created >= "2023-01-01"'\n- Content with specific label: 'label=documentation'\n- Recently modified content: 'lastModified > startOfMonth("-1M")'\n- Content modified this year: 'creator = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfYear()'\n- Content you contributed to recently: 'contributor = currentUser() AND lastModified > startOfWeek()'\n- Content watched by user: 'watcher = "user@domain.com" AND type = page'\n- Exact phrase in content: 'text ~ "\\"Urgent Review Required\\"" AND label = "pending-approval"'\n- Title wildcards: 'title ~ "Minutes*" AND (space = "HR" OR space = "Marketing")'\nNote: Special identifiers need proper quoting in CQL: personal space keys (e.g., "~username"), reserved words, numeric IDs, and identifiers with special characters.

ok If provided, fetches the file content from this URL. Supports http:// and https://; file:// only where local file access is enabled. Where it is disabled, files on the caller's machine go through an upload URL instead (see the upload-URL parameter, if offered).
ok Smart chip(s) to insert instead of values: - A single URL or email string for a single cell (e.g., "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/123", "user@example.com"). - A list of URLs or emails for a single cell (multiple chips) or across cells (e.g., ["https://...", "https://..."]). - A 2D list of URLs/emails matching a grid range. For a single-row or single-column range, each inner list is instead the chips for one cell (e.g., [["a@x.com", "b@x.com"]] puts both chips in the first cell of "A1:C1"). - A dict or list of dicts with explicit properties (e.g., {"type": "drive", "uri": "..."}, {"type": "person", "email": "..."}). - A JSON-encoded string representing any of the above formats.
ok Optional RFC Message-ID to explicitly reply to a specific message (e.g., '<message123@gmail.com>'). Omit to reply to the latest eligible message in thread_id.
ok Optional list of attachments. Each can have: "url" (fetch from URL — works with MCP attachment URLs from get_drive_file_download_url / get_gmail_attachment_content), OR "path" (file path, auto-encodes), OR "content" (standard base64, not urlsafe) + "filename". Optional "mime_type". Optional "content_id" (string) makes the attachment inline-rendered: it lands in a multipart/related part with `Content-ID: <content_id>` and `Content-Disposition: inline`, and the HTML body can reference it via `<img src="cid:<content_id>">` (RFC 2392). Without `content_id` the attachment is a regular multipart/mixed attachment. Example: [{"url": "https://host/attachments/abc-123", "filename": "report.pdf"}]
